questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011 which one of the following Union Territories had the highest sex ratio?
questions.questionHtml: According to the Census of India 2011 which one of the following Union Territories had the highest sex ratio?
questions.solution: According to the Census of India 2011, Puducherry had the highest sex ratio among Union Territories, with 1,038 females per 1,000 males. This information highlights Puducherry's favorable gender balance compared to other Union Territories.

questions.question: In which of the following years was India’s population growth negative?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years was India’s population growth negative?
questions.solution: India’s population growth was negative in the year 1921. This was due to significant mortality caused by famines, epidemics, and particularly the influenza pandemic of 1918, which led to a decline in population growth between 1911 and 1921.

questions.question: Which of the following is among the ‘pull factors of migration’?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is among the ‘pull factors of migration’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Security of life.

Important Points

  • Migration is another way by which the population size changes apart from birth and death.
  • Migration is an integral part of redistributing population over time and space.
  • Migration can be permanent, temporary, or seasonal.
  • Migration may take place from rural to rural areas, rural to urban areas, urban to urban areas, and urban to rural areas.
  • People migrate from one place to another for a better economic and social life.
  • The two sets of factors that influence migration are:
    1. The push factors
    2. The pull factor.

Key Points 

  • The Pull factors make the place of destination seem more attractive than the place of origin for reasons such as:
    • Better job opportunities and living conditions.
    • Peace and stability.
    • Security of life and property.
    • Pleasant climate
  • The Push factors make the place of origin seem less attractive for reasons such as:
    • Unemployment.
    • Poor living conditions.
    • Political turmoil.
    • Unpleasant climate.
    • Natural disasters.
    • Epidemics and socio-economic backwardness.

questions.solution: As per the 2011 census, the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in India was approximately 2.1 to 2.9. This range indicates the average number of children expected to be born to a woman during her reproductive years in India during that time.

questions.question: Before ______, India was in the first stage of demographic transition.
questions.questionHtml: Before ______, India was in the first stage of demographic transition.
questions.solution: Before 1921, India was in the first stage of a demographic transition, characterized by high birth and death rates, resulting in a stable population. In 1921, known as the "Year of the Great Divide," India experienced a demographic shift with declining death rates while birth rates remained high, marking the transition to the second stage. This stage is characterized by rapid population growth due to healthcare, sanitation, and food supply improvements.

questions.question: In which decade negative growth rate in India’s population found?
questions.questionHtml: In which decade negative growth rate in India’s population found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1911-1921.

Key Points

  • Nearly 65 lakh people died from the plague between 1901 and 1911.
    • The plague was far more prevalent in towns than in rural areas.
  • There were 954 females per 1,000 males in 1911 as compared to 963 females per 1,000 males in 1901.
    • The report says that this decrease was due to female mortality as a result of epidemics such as plague and malaria.
  • Due to the occurrence of influenza in 1918, the mortality rate of the country increased and caused 1.4 crore deaths in the country.
  • In addition, the occurrence of famine, plague, and malaria also resulted in the decline of the population.
  • All of these resulted in a significant decline in population leading to a negative growth rate.
  • The census year 1911- 1921 registered a negative growth rate of-0.31 percent which happened only once throughout the demographic history of India.

Additional Information

  • The decennial Census of India has been conducted 15 times, as of 2011.
  • It has been undertaken every 10 years, after the first complete census was undertaken in 1881 under Viceroy Lord Ripon.
  • The first unofficial census was undertaken in 1872 under British Viceroy Lord Mayo.
